title: How does the power line of seven solve eight calculations?
description: Eight calculations are solved with the power line of seven, the same way as the worked example in the book. Each number is read as a power of seven, and then the exponents are added, taken away or multiplied.
teaching_notes: One idea: read each number on the power line as a power of seven, then work only with the exponents. Watch for students who add the exponents when dividing, or who lose the minus sign on a negative exponent.

source: Power lines: the power line of 7
video_script.why: A learner reads numbers off a power line as powers of one base and moves along the line by adding or taking away exponents, the same way as the worked example on the power line of four.
video_script.substitution: the book's own power line of seven and its eight calculations
video_script.anchor: the power line of seven with eight calculations written below it
video_script.payoff_line: Multiplying adds the exponents, dividing takes them away, and a power of a power multiplies them

final_answer.value: 7 to the power 6, 7 to the power 6, 7 to the power 7, 7³, 7 to the power −2, 7 to the power −2, 7³, and 7 to the power −6
final_answer.spoken: seven to the power six, seven to the power six, seven to the power seven, seven cubed, seven to the power negative two, seven to the power negative two, seven cubed, and seven to the power negative six

video_script.design: One idea: read each number on the power line as a power of seven, then work with the exponents. The last answer, 7^-6, stays hidden until the answer; a number check closes the working.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Use the power line for seven to find these eight.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Two thousand four hundred and one times forty nine.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Forty nine cubed.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Three hundred and forty three times two thousand four hundred and one.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Sixteen thousand eight hundred and seven divided by forty nine.
<bookmark mark='e'/>Seven divided by three hundred and forty three.
<bookmark mark='f'/>Sixteen thousand eight hundred and seven divided by eight lakh twenty three thousand five hundred and forty three.
<bookmark mark='g'/>One lakh seventeen thousand six hundred and forty nine times one over three hundred and forty three.
<bookmark mark='h'/>One over three hundred and forty three, times one over three hundred and forty three.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write each as a power of seven.

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: power line of 7: 7^1 = 7, 7^2 = 49, 7^3 = 343, 7^4 = 2401, 7^5 = 16807, 7^6 = 117649, 7^7 = 823543; rule cards for times, divided and power of a power

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='line'/>The power line lists seven to the powers one to seven.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Times adds the exponents, and divided takes them away.

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the power line for seven, and eight calculations.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each answer as a power of seven.

marks.one: 2401 is found at 7^4 and 49 at 7^2 on the line

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, part one. Two thousand four hundred and one is seven to the power four.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Forty nine is seven squared, and four plus two is six.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Part two, forty nine cubed is seven squared, all cubed. Two times three is six.

marks.three: 343 is found at 7^3 and 2401 at 7^4; 3 + 4 = 7 gives 7^7
marks.four: 16807 is found at 7^5 and 49 at 7^2; 5 - 2 = 3 gives 7^3

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step two, part three. Three hundred and forty three is seven cubed. Three plus four gives seven.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Part four, sixteen thousand eight hundred and seven is seven to the power five. Five take away two is three.

marks.five: 7 is found at 7^1 and 343 at 7^3; 1 - 3 = -2 gives 7^-2
marks.six: 16807 is found at 7^5 and 823543 at 7^7; 5 - 7 = -2 gives 7^-2

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step three, part five. Seven is seven to the power one, and three hundred and forty three is seven cubed. One take away three is negative two.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Part six, eight lakh twenty three thousand five hundred and forty three is seven to the power seven. Five take away seven is negative two.

marks.eight: 7^-3 x 7^-3 is written with -3 + (-3) in the exponent

narration: <bookmark mark='seven'/>Step four, part seven. One lakh seventeen thousand six hundred and forty nine is seven to the power six.
<bookmark mark='inv'/>One over three hundred and forty three is seven to the power negative three. Six plus negative three is three.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>Part eight is seven to the power negative three, twice. Negative three plus negative three is negative six.

marks.chk: 7 / 343 = 1/49 is written and matches 7^-2 from part five

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step five, check part five with numbers. Seven divided by three hundred and forty three is one over forty nine. That is seven to the power negative two.
